questions.question: Which statement best discriminates '(M+2) Isotope Peak' from other related principles in Infrared Spectroscopy and Mass Spectrometry?

options.label: A
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, (M+2) Isotope Peak specifically denotes: A diagnostic mass spectral peak two mass units heavier than the molecular ion that reveals the presence of elements with prominent isotopes (e.g., Cl in 3:1 ratio, Br in 1:1 ratio).

options.label: B
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, (M+2) Isotope Peak is properly defined as: The high-wavenumber zone of an IR spectrum (1500–4000 cm⁻¹) containing clear, characteristic absorption bands for major functional groups (O-H, N-H, C≡C, C=O).

options.label: C
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, (M+2) Isotope Peak is properly defined as: An analytical technique that measures the absorption of infrared radiation corresponding to quantized vibrational transitions (stretches and bends) in covalent bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: Unlike related phenomena, (M+2) Isotope Peak is properly defined as: The reciprocal of wavelength (1/λ) expressed in units of cm⁻¹, directly proportional to the vibrational frequency and energy of the absorbed radiation.
